knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality and error bounds for an inverse polynomial solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives global-minimizer and objective-gap guarantees for an optimal solution of the degree-bounded inverse problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\mathbf K\) has nonempty interior, \(\mathbf x^*\in\mathbf K\) globally minimizes \(\mathbf P\) with value \(f^*\), and \(\widetilde f_d\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_{d_0}\) optimally solves \(\mathbf P_d\) with value \(\rho_d^k\). Then \(0\in\mathbf K\) globally minimizes \(\widetilde f_d\) over \(\mathbf K\). If \(\rho_d^k=0\), then \(\widetilde f_d=f\) and \(0\) globally minimizes \(\mathbf P\). For \(k=1\), \[f^*\le f(0)\le f^*+\rho_d^1\sup_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{d_0}^n}|(\mathbf x^*)^\alpha|,\] which becomes \(f^*\le f(0)\le f^*+\rho_d^1\) when \(\mathbf K\subseteq[-1,1]^n\). For \(k=\infty\), \[f^*\le f(0)\le f^*+\rho_d^\infty\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{d_0}^n}|(\mathbf x^*)^\alpha|,\] which becomes \(f^*\le f(0)\le f^*+s(d_0)\rho_d^\infty\) when \(\mathbf K\subseteq[-1,1]^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under nonempty-interior and attainment assumptions, zero is a global minimizer of the optimized inverse polynomial. A zero inverse objective recovers the original polynomial and makes zero globally optimal for the original problem. For the 1-norm and infinity-norm inverse formulations, the theorem also bounds the original objective gap at zero, with simpler bounds when K lies in the unit box.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf x\in\mathbf K}f(\mathbf x),\quad f^*=f(\mathbf x^*)
\widetilde f_d\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_{d_0}\text{ optimally solves }\mathbf P_d\text{ with value }\rho_d^k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf x\in\mathbf K}\widetilde f_d(\mathbf x);\quad \rho_d^k=0\Rightarrow \widetilde f_d=f\text{ and }0\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf x\in\mathbf K}f(\mathbf x).\quad k=1\Rightarrow f^*\le f(0)\le f^*+\rho_d^1\sup_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{d_0}^n}|(\mathbf x^*)^\alpha|;\quad k=\infty\Rightarrow f^*\le f(0)\le f^*+\rho_d^\infty\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{d_0}^n}|(\mathbf x^*)^\alpha|,\text{ with the stated unit-box simplifications.}

assumptions_latex: An AC network has bus-admittance matrix \(Y=G+\mathrm{i}B\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Active and reactive power injections are quadratic polynomials in the rectangular voltage coordinates \((e,f)\).

notation.meaning: real and imaginary voltage components at bus i
active and reactive net power injections

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rectangular-voltage AC power-balance equations are quadratic polynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bus-injection AC power flow using rectangular voltages and the load-sign convention \(S_i=V_i\overline{(YV)_i}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(V_i=e_i+\mathrm{i}f_i\), \(Y_{ij}=G_{ij}+\mathrm{i}B_{ij}\), and \(S_i=P_i+\mathrm{i}Q_i:=V_i\overline{(YV)_i}\), the bus injections satisfy \[P_i=\sum_j\bigl(G_{ij}(e_ie_j+f_if_j)+B_{ij}(f_ie_j-e_if_j)\bigr),\] \[Q_i=\sum_j\bigl(G_{ij}(f_ie_j-e_if_j)-B_{ij}(e_ie_j+f_if_j)\bigr).\] Moreover, \(|V_i|^2=e_i^2+f_i^2\). Consequently, power-balance equations, squared-voltage bounds, and polynomial generation costs yield a real polynomial OPF formulation after substituting these expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Writing each complex bus voltage by real and imaginary parts converts AC power injections and squared voltage magnitudes into real quadratic polynomials.
knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular-Voltage Polynomial Formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed rectangular-coordinate injection formulas are algebraically consistent with the stated convention S_i=V_i overline{(YV)_i}, and representation is the correct content kind. An AC-OPF source is required to verify the network and sign conventions and to support the claimed formulation scope.

assumptions_latex: An AC network has complex bus-admittance matrix \(Y\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bus injections and squared voltage magnitudes are Hermitian quadratic forms in \(V\), equivalently linear trace expressions in \(W=VV^*\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: complex AC injections admit Hermitian quadratic and lifted trace representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complex-voltage bus-injection representation and its rank-one Hermitian matrix lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_i=e_ie_i^{\mathsf T}\) select bus \(i\), and define \(A_i:=Y^*E_i\). Under \(S_i=P_i+\mathrm{i}Q_i:=V_i\overline{(YV)_i}\), one has \[S_i=V^*A_iV,\qquad P_i=V^*\frac{A_i+A_i^*}{2}V,\qquad Q_i=V^*\frac{A_i-A_i^*}{2\mathrm{i}}V.\] Also \(|V_i|^2=V^*E_iV\). With \(W:=VV^*\), these quantities become linear trace expressions \(\operatorname{tr}(A_iW)\), \(\operatorname{tr}((A_i+A_i^*)W/2)\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(E_iW)\), subject to \(W\succeq 0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(W)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complex AC power quantities are Hermitian quadratic forms in voltage and become linear trace expressions after the rank-one lift to a voltage matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Complex-Voltage Hermitian Formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hermitian quadratic identities and rank-one lift are algebraically consistent with the stated bus-injection convention, and representation is the correct knowledge kind. No inspectable AC-OPF source is supplied to confirm the matrix convention and formulation context.

knowledge_statements.title: Current–Voltage Polynomial Formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular-coordinate current–voltage representation of a steady-state AC network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every directed branch \((i,j)\), introduce complex bus voltages \(V_i\) and branch currents \(I_{ij}\). With fixed series admittance \(y_{ij}\), charging admittance \(y_{ij}^{\mathrm{sh}}\), and nonzero transformer ratio \(t_{ij}\), impose \[I_{ij}=(y_{ij}+y_{ij}^{\mathrm{sh}})V_i-y_{ij}V_j/t_{ij}.\] Define sending-end power by \(S_{ij}=P_{ij}+\mathrm{i}Q_{ij}=V_i\overline{I_{ij}}\). After writing \(V_i=e_i+\mathrm{i}f_i\) and \(I_{ij}=a_{ij}+\mathrm{i}b_{ij}\), the current equations are affine and \(P_{ij}=e_i a_{ij}+f_i b_{ij}\), \(Q_{ij}=f_i a_{ij}-e_i b_{ij}\) are quadratic real polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch currents are affine in endpoint voltages, while active and reactive powers are quadratic products of rectangular voltage and current components.
assumptions_latex: All network admittances and transformer ratios are fixed data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The AC branch equations admit a real polynomial formulation of degree at most two in rectangular current and voltage variables.

notation.meaning: Complex voltage and its rectangular components at bus i.
Directed branch current and its rectangular components.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard rectangular AC branch equations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, and the rectangular power identities are internally consistent. However, the stated branch-current law depends on transformer-tap and charging-admittance conventions; complex taps commonly require conjugation and direction-specific coefficients. No inspectable OPF citation is supplied to establish this exact convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Bus–Branch Network Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static input data defining the polynomial AC OPF network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Bus–branch network data consist of a finite bus set \(N\), a directed-arc set \(A\) containing orientations of physical branches, a generator set \(G\), and an incidence map \(\beta:G\to N\). Each bus \(i\) has fixed demand \(S_i^d\), shunt admittance \(y_i^{\mathrm{sh}}\), and voltage bounds \(0\leq \underline v_i\leq \overline v_i\). Each arc \((i,j)\) has series admittance, charging data, transformer ratio, and applicable current, apparent-power, or angle-difference limits. Each generator has active-power, reactive-power, and cost data. These constants parameterize, but are not decision variables of, the OPF polynomial system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The network input specifies buses, branches, generators, their incidence, electrical parameters, demands, operating bounds, and generation costs.
assumptions_latex: Every generator is assigned to exactly one bus by \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tuple of sets, incidence maps, electrical constants, bounds, demands, and costs uniquely parameterizes the chosen static AC OPF instance.

notation.meaning: Fixed complex demand at bus i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional static AC OPF data model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the network-data leaf. The listed data are plausible, but branch orientations, charging parameters, transformer data, optional limits, and cost representations vary among AC OPF data models. An authoritative source with a specific model-definition locator is required.

children.title: Voltage Variables
children.top_down_role: Voltage magnitude, component, or phasor variables used in polynomial OPF models.

knowledge_statements.title: Voltage Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular bus-voltage decision variables for polynomial OPF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each bus \(i\in N\), the voltage variable is the complex phasor \(V_i=e_i+\mathrm{i}f_i\), represented in a real polynomial model by the pair \((e_i,f_i)\in\mathbb R^2\). Its squared magnitude is the quadratic polynomial \(|V_i|^2=e_i^2+f_i^2\). When polar quantities are used only for interpretation, \(|V_i|=(e_i^2+f_i^2)^{1/2}\) and \(\arg V_i\) are derived quantities rather than additional polynomial decision variables. One rotational degree of freedom must be normalized on each connected network component unless absolute phasor data fix it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each bus voltage is represented by two real variables; squared magnitude is quadratic, while magnitude and angle are derived quantities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The voltage block is \((e,f)\in\mathbb R^{2|N|}\), with every squared voltage magnitude polynomial in that block.

notation.meaning: Complex voltage phasor at bus i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the variable-taxonomy leaf, and the rectangular parametrization and squared-magnitude identity are precise. The added componentwise gauge-normalization claim is model-dependent and has no inspectable source supporting its hypotheses and scope.

children.title: Generation Variables
children.top_down_role: Active-power or reactive-power generation variables at controllable buses.

knowledge_statements.title: Generation Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active and reactive generator-output variables in AC OPF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every generator \(g\in G\), define the complex generation variable \(S_g^G=P_g^G+\mathrm{i}Q_g^G\), represented by \((P_g^G,Q_g^G)\in\mathbb R^2\). Standard box limits impose \(\underline P_g\leq P_g^G\leq\overline P_g\) and \(\underline Q_g\leq Q_g^G\leq\overline Q_g\). At bus \(i\), aggregate generation is \(S_i^G=\sum_{g:\,\beta(g)=i}S_g^G\). Thus generation variables enter nodal power balance linearly, although polynomial costs or coupled capability constraints may introduce higher-degree expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each generator has real active- and reactive-power outputs, bounded individually and summed by bus for use in power balance.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g\in G\) has finite prescribed output bounds.
\(\beta:G\to N\) assigns each generator to one bus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Generator injections form a real variable block whose bus aggregates are linear functions of individual outputs.

notation.meaning: Active and reactive output of generator g.
Aggregate complex generation at bus i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional AC OPF generator variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, and the aggregation map is mathematically clear. No cited AC OPF formulation verifies the sign convention, generator bounds, and claimed linear appearance in the intended polynomial template.

children.title: Branch-Flow Variables
children.top_down_role: Power-flow or current-related variables associated with network branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Flow Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed current and complex-power variables associated with network branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each directed arc \((i,j)\in A\), branch-flow variables may comprise the complex current \(I_{ij}=a_{ij}+\mathrm{i}b_{ij}\) and complex sending-end power \(S_{ij}=P_{ij}+\mathrm{i}Q_{ij}\). They are linked to endpoint voltages by the affine branch-current law and the quadratic identities \(P_{ij}=e_i a_{ij}+f_i b_{ij}\) and \(Q_{ij}=f_i a_{ij}-e_i b_{ij}\). Variables for opposite orientations are distinct because line losses generally imply \(S_{ij}+S_{ji}\neq0\). Current or apparent-power limits can then be expressed using \(a_{ij}^2+b_{ij}^2\) or \(P_{ij}^2+Q_{ij}^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directed branch variables record current and power; polynomial equations couple them to endpoint voltages, and opposite-direction powers need not cancel.
assumptions_latex: Every physical branch has the directed orientations required by the formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branch-current and branch-power variables can be coupled to voltages by affine and quadratic polynomial equations.

notation.meaning: Current directed from bus i toward bus j.
Complex power directed from bus i toward bus j.
Rectangular voltage components at the sending bus.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard directed AC branch-flow variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the branch-flow variable leaf, and the voltage-current power identities are consistent. Whether both current and power are explicit variables, how reverse arcs are represented, and which terminal limits apply are formulation-specific and unsupported by an inspectable citation.

children.title: Cross-Element Variable Coupling
children.top_down_role: Variable dependencies spanning buses, generators, and incident branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Element Variable Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparsity pattern induced by buses, generators, and incident branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a bus–branch AC OPF formulation, each generator variable couples to the voltage and balance equations of its assigned bus, while each directed branch equation couples only its branch variables and the voltages at its two endpoint buses. Nodal balance at bus \(i\) couples the aggregate generation at \(i\), fixed demand, bus voltage, and flows on arcs incident to \(i\). Consequently, two nonincident branches or generators at different nonadjacent buses share no constraint unless an additional system-wide operating constraint or objective term is introduced. The resulting polynomial correlative-sparsity graph is therefore generated by bus neighborhoods and any explicitly imposed global constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: OPF coupling is local: generators meet their buses, branches meet their endpoints, and nodal balance joins variables incident to one bus.
assumptions_latex: The model contains only standard branch laws, nodal balances, local bounds, and separable generator costs.
No additional system-wide coupling constraint is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The support of each standard OPF polynomial lies within one bus neighborhood or one branch endpoint pair.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incidence-induced sparsity of network polynomial models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the coupling leaf. The locality claim is plausible under the stated restricted model, but the exact correlative-sparsity conclusion depends on the chosen polynomial encoding, treatment of branch variables, and objective representation. No source verifies that scope.

children.title: Reference-Bus Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of the network bus used to anchor voltage-angle coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference-Bus Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule for removing independent voltage-angle symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the bus–branch graph have connected components \(N_1,\ldots,N_c\). A valid reference-bus set is a subset \(R\subseteq N\) satisfying \(|R\cap N_k|=1\) for every \(k=1,\ldots,c\), provided each selected reference voltage is constrained away from zero. If the graph is connected, this reduces to choosing one bus \(r\in N\). Selecting no reference in a component leaves its common voltage angle undetermined; selecting multiple references is permissible only when their prescribed angles are mutually compatible and is unnecessary for eliminating the rotational gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one nonzero-voltage reference bus in every connected network component; a connected network therefore needs one reference bus.
assumptions_latex: The network topology and its connected components are fixed.
Each selected reference bus satisfies a positive lower voltage-magnitude bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one selected reference per connected component removes each independent common-angle degree of freedom without overconstraining relative angles.

notation.meaning: Connected components of the bus graph.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: one rotational gauge per connected component

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf. One reference per independently rotational component is standard, but the assertion about multiple references and compatible prescribed angles requires a precise distinction between redundant gauge choices and constraints on relative phase. No authoritative source is cited for the stated version.

children.title: Voltage-Angle Normalization
children.top_down_role: Coordinate conventions fixing the global voltage-angle reference.

knowledge_statements.title: Voltage-Angle Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial reference-angle constraint in rectangular voltage coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a selected reference bus \(r\) with \(|V_r|>0\), the normalization \(\arg V_r=0\) is represented in rectangular coordinates by \(f_r=0\) and \(e_r\geq0\). If the voltage lower bound satisfies \(\underline v_r>0\), feasibility strengthens the latter relation to \(e_r\geq\underline v_r>0\). The equality \(f_r=0\) alone is insufficient because it also permits angle \(\pi\) when \(e_r<0\). Applying this condition once in each connected component selects a representative of every orbit under common complex rotation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set the reference voltage’s imaginary part to zero and require a nonnegative real part, thereby selecting angle zero rather than angle pi.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraints \(f_r=0\) and \(e_r\geq0\) impose the reference angle \(\arg V_r=0\) without trigonometric variables.

notation.meaning: Rectangular voltage at the reference bus.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, and the distinction between f_r=0 alone and f_r=0 with e_r nonnegative is mathematically sound for a nonzero reference voltage. An inspectable source is still needed to support this exact polynomial gauge convention in the intended OPF model.

children.title: Rotational Gauge Freedom
children.top_down_role: Global phase symmetry motivating reference-coordinate normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Rotational Gauge Freedom
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-phase invariance of AC network equations without absolute phasor constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an AC OPF model depends on voltages and currents only through voltage magnitudes, products \(V_i\overline{V_j}\), products \(V_i\overline{I_{ij}}\), and linear network equations. For any \(\phi\in\mathbb R\), transform \(V_i' = e^{\mathrm{i}\phi}V_i\) and \(I_{ij}'=e^{\mathrm{i}\phi}I_{ij}\), leaving active and reactive generation unchanged. Every voltage magnitude and complex-power product is invariant, and the linear current equations rotate consistently. Hence feasibility and any objective depending only on power or voltage magnitude are unchanged. Each connected component admits an independent rotation unless another constraint couples its absolute phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common phase rotation of all voltages and currents in a connected component preserves powers, magnitudes, feasibility, and standard OPF objectives.
assumptions_latex: No constraint or objective term fixes an absolute voltage or current phase.
Network equations are homogeneous under simultaneous complex rotation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformation \((V,I)\mapsto(e^{\mathrm{i}\phi}V,e^{\mathrm{i}\phi}I)\) is a symmetry of the standard AC OPF model.

notation.meaning: Bus voltage and directed branch current phasors.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: global phase symmetry of AC power equations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the gauge-freedom leaf. The symmetry claim is plausible under homogeneous network equations and absence of absolute-phase terms, but no cited formulation confirms that all constraints and objective terms in scope satisfy those hypotheses.

children.title: Normalization Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Degenerate or disconnected network regimes requiring special reference treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cases where a single reference-angle constraint is invalid or insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A single-bus angle normalization fails to remove all gauge freedom when the bus graph has at least two disconnected components: rotating any unreferenced component independently preserves its standard AC equations. Angle normalization is undefined at a selected bus with \(V_r=0\), because \(\arg V_r\) has no value; algebraically, \(f_r=0\) then does not select a unique rotational orbit. Conversely, imposing a reference-angle constraint can change the feasible set when the model includes an absolute phasor measurement, externally synchronized phase condition, or another term that is not invariant under common rotation. Gauge fixing is valid only for genuine, componentwise rotational symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One reference is insufficient for disconnected networks, zero reference voltage has no angle, and normalization is invalid when absolute-phase data already break symmetry.
assumptions_latex: The intended normalization fixes one selected bus angle.
The underlying model may be disconnected or contain absolute-phase information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reference-angle normalization is sound only when every rotationally free component has a nonzero reference and no imposed constraint conflicts with the chosen phase.

notation.meaning: Voltage at the selected reference bus.
Reference voltage angle, defined only for nonzero voltage.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary boundaries of phase-gauge fixing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind exactly fits the leaf, and the listed disconnected-network, zero-voltage, and absolute-phase cases are coherent. Their precise applicability depends on the underlying model's component structure and phase-sensitive data, for which no inspectable source is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Power-Balance Polynomial Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular-voltage nodal active and reactive power balance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=G+\mathrm{i}B\) be the bus-admittance matrix and \(V_i=e_i+\mathrm{i}f_i\). At every bus \(i\), impose \[\sum_{g:\,\beta(g)=i}P_g^G-P_i^d=\sum_{k\in N}\bigl(G_{ik}(e_i e_k+f_i f_k)+B_{ik}(f_i e_k-e_i f_k)\bigr),\] \[\sum_{g:\,\beta(g)=i}Q_g^G-Q_i^d=\sum_{k\in N}\bigl(G_{ik}(f_i e_k-e_i f_k)-B_{ik}(e_i e_k+f_i f_k)\bigr).\] These equations are the real and imaginary parts of \(\sum_{g:\,\beta(g)=i}S_g^G-S_i^d=V_i\overline{\sum_kY_{ik}V_k}\) and are polynomial of degree at most two.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each bus, generation minus demand equals the admittance-based voltage injection; rectangular coordinates make both active and reactive balances quadratic polynomials.
assumptions_latex: The bus-admittance matrix includes the modeled branch and shunt admittances.
Demand and network parameters are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nodal active- and reactive-power balance is expressible as two real quadratic polynomial equalities per bus.

notation.meaning: Complex bus-admittance matrix and its real and imaginary parts.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard rectangular AC nodal-balance expansion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, and the displayed real and reactive balance expansions are algebraically consistent with the stated complex equation. The signs nevertheless depend on the bus-admittance and injection conventions, so an authoritative OPF source with the exact convention and a specific locator is required.

children.title: Voltage-Magnitude Limit Models
children.top_down_role: Polynomial constraints representing admissible bus-voltage magnitude ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Voltage-Magnitude Limit Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial lower and upper bounds on bus-voltage magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each bus \(i\in N\), let \(0\leq\underline v_i\leq\overline v_i\) be prescribed voltage-magnitude limits and write \(V_i=e_i+\mathrm{i}f_i\). The admissible voltage annulus is defined exactly by \[(\underline v_i)^2\leq e_i^2+f_i^2\leq(\overline v_i)^2.\] Equivalently, use the polynomial inequalities \(e_i^2+f_i^2-(\underline v_i)^2\geq0\) and \((\overline v_i)^2-e_i^2-f_i^2\geq0\). The lower inequality is nonconvex when \(\underline v_i>0\), whereas the upper inequality defines a convex disk in the rectangular voltage plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squaring the voltage-magnitude bounds yields two exact quadratic inequalities in the real and imaginary voltage components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Voltage-magnitude limits are represented exactly by two quadratic polynomial inequalities per bus.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact squared-magnitude reformulation in rectangular coordinates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, and the squared-magnitude inequalities, exactness conditions, and convexity statements are mathematically precise. The record supplies only standard-field rationale and no authoritative section or page tying this condition to the intended AC OPF polynomial template.

children.title: Active-Generation Limit Models
children.top_down_role: Polynomial constraints representing active-power generation ranges.

assumptions_latex: For each bus \(i\), the voltage is \(V_i=e_i+\mathrm{i}f_i\), and the network admittance matrix is \(Y=G+\mathrm{i}B\).
The active demand \(P_i^d\) and generation bounds \(\underline P_i^g,\overline P_i^g\) are fixed real data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline P_i^g\le P_i^g(e,f)\le\overline P_i^g\) is a pair of polynomial inequalities.

notation.meaning: Rectangular voltage components at bus i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rectangular-coordinate AC power-injection equations give quadratic active-generation polynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular-voltage formulation with fixed active demand and finite generator bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every generator bus \(i\), define the active-generation polynomial by \[P_i^g(e,f)=P_i^d+e_i\sum_k(G_{ik}e_k-B_{ik}f_k)+f_i\sum_k(B_{ik}e_k+G_{ik}f_k).\] The active-generation operating limits are the polynomial constraints \[P_i^g(e,f)-\underline P_i^g\ge0,\qquad \overline P_i^g-P_i^g(e,f)\ge0.\] At a bus without controllable active generation, the same model is obtained by setting \(\underline P_i^g=\overline P_i^g\) to its prescribed value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active generation equals fixed demand plus the quadratic network injection, and its lower and upper operating bounds become polynomial inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Generation Limit Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the Active-Generation Limit Models leaf and is mathematically plausible under the stated admittance convention. However, no inspectable citation supports the injection formula, sign convention, or treatment of nongenerator buses; the unrelated local inventory cannot establish these details.

children.title: Reactive-Generation Limit Models
children.top_down_role: Polynomial constraints representing reactive-power generation ranges.

assumptions_latex: For each bus \(i\), the voltage is \(V_i=e_i+\mathrm{i}f_i\), and the network admittance matrix is \(Y=G+\mathrm{i}B\).
The reactive demand \(Q_i^d\) and generation bounds \(\underline Q_i^g,\overline Q_i^g\) are fixed real data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline Q_i^g\le Q_i^g(e,f)\le\overline Q_i^g\) is a pair of polynomial inequalities.

notation.meaning: Rectangular voltage components at bus i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rectangular-coordinate AC power-injection equations give quadratic reactive-generation polynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular-voltage formulation with fixed reactive demand and finite generator bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every generator bus \(i\), define the reactive-generation polynomial by \[Q_i^g(e,f)=Q_i^d+f_i\sum_k(G_{ik}e_k-B_{ik}f_k)-e_i\sum_k(B_{ik}e_k+G_{ik}f_k).\] The reactive-generation operating limits are the polynomial constraints \[Q_i^g(e,f)-\underline Q_i^g\ge0,\qquad \overline Q_i^g-Q_i^g(e,f)\ge0.\] At a bus without controllable reactive generation, equality to a prescribed value is represented by coincident lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reactive generation equals fixed demand plus the quadratic network injection, and its lower and upper bounds become polynomial inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Reactive-Generation Limit Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the Reactive-Generation Limit Models leaf and the displayed formula is plausible under a standard admittance convention. An authoritative OPF source with a specific locator is required to establish the reactive-power signs and the coincident-bound modeling convention.

children.title: Coupled Operating-Limit Regimes
children.top_down_role: OPF regimes where voltage restrictions interact with generator capability limits.

assumptions_latex: The voltage, active-generation, and reactive-generation limits are expressed as polynomial inequalities in rectangular voltage variables.
All lower and upper bounds are fixed finite data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The joint voltage-generation operating region is a basic closed semialgebraic set.

notation.meaning: Squared voltage magnitude at bus i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: intersections of polynomial bound constraints are basic closed semialgebraic sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint enforcement of voltage-magnitude and active-reactive generation bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each bus \(i\), let \(w_i=e_i^2+f_i^2\). The coupled voltage-generation operating region is \[\mathcal O=\left\{(e,f):\ \underline V_i^2\le w_i\le\overline V_i^2,\ \underline P_i^g\le P_i^g(e,f)\le\overline P_i^g,\ \underline Q_i^g\le Q_i^g(e,f)\le\overline Q_i^g\ \text{for every }i\right\}.\] Splitting every two-sided bound into two one-sided polynomial inequalities represents \(\mathcal O\) as a basic closed semialgebraic set and preserves the coupling induced by the common voltage variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneously imposing voltage, active-generation, and reactive-generation bounds produces a basic closed semialgebraic operating region in the shared voltage variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Operating-Limit Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the appropriate knowledge kind, and an intersection of polynomial bound constraints is basic closed semialgebraic. The statement nevertheless applies generation bounds "for every" bus without defining the applicable bus sets or nongenerator convention, and it cites no source for the underlying OPF constraints.

children.title: Branch-Flow Polynomial Models
children.top_down_role: Polynomial representations of power or current flow on network branches.

assumptions_latex: Each directed branch \((i,j)\) has series admittance \(y_{ij}=g_{ij}+\mathrm{i}b_{ij}\) and sending-end shunt admittance \(y_{ij}^{\mathrm{sh}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both \(P_{ij}\) and \(Q_{ij}\) are real quadratic polynomials in the endpoint voltage components.

notation.meaning: Complex power sent from bus i toward bus j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the rectangular-coordinate pi-model yields quadratic branch-power polynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed branch-flow representation for a series-plus-shunt line without an off-nominal transformer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a directed branch \((i,j)\), define \[I_{ij}=y_{ij}(V_i-V_j)+y_{ij}^{\mathrm{sh}}V_i,\qquad S_{ij}=V_i\overline{I_{ij}}=P_{ij}+\mathrm{i}Q_{ij}.\] After substituting \(V_i=e_i+\mathrm{i}f_i\) and \(V_j=e_j+\mathrm{i}f_j\), the real and imaginary parts \(P_{ij}(e,f)\) and \(Q_{ij}(e,f)\) are real polynomials of degree at most two involving only the voltage components at buses \(i\) and \(j\). Reverse-end flow is obtained independently from \(S_{ji}=V_j\overline{I_{ji}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complex branch power is voltage times conjugate current; in rectangular coordinates, each directed active and reactive flow is quadratic in endpoint voltages.
knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Flow Polynomial Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the branch-flow leaf and is correct for the explicitly scoped series-plus-sending-shunt model without an off-nominal transformer. A branch-model source with a specific locator is still necessary because shunt allocation, direction, conjugation, and transformer conventions materially affect the formula.

children.title: Thermal Limit Models
children.top_down_role: Polynomial constraints representing branch thermal ratings.

assumptions_latex: Directed branch powers \(P_{ij}(e,f)\) and \(Q_{ij}(e,f)\) follow the branch-flow polynomial model.
The apparent-power rating \(\overline S_{ij}\) is fixed and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sending-end thermal limit is the quartic polynomial inequality \(\overline S_{ij}^{\,2}-P_{ij}^2-Q_{ij}^2\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Directed active and reactive branch flows

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: apparent-power ratings are imposed through squared flow magnitude
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Apparent-power thermal rating imposed separately at each monitored branch end.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The apparent-power thermal limit at the sending end of directed branch \((i,j)\) is \[|S_{ij}|\le\overline S_{ij}.\] Because \(|S_{ij}|^2=P_{ij}(e,f)^2+Q_{ij}(e,f)^2\), its polynomial form is \[\overline S_{ij}^{\,2}-P_{ij}(e,f)^2-Q_{ij}(e,f)^2\ge0.\] When both ends are rated, the analogous inequality with \((j,i)\) must also hold. If the branch-flow components are quadratic, each resulting thermal constraint has degree at most four in the rectangular voltage variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An apparent-power rating becomes a quartic polynomial inequality obtained by bounding the sum of squared active and reactive branch flows.
knowledge_statements.title: Thermal Limit Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is appropriate for this leaf, and the squared apparent-power inequality is standard. The conclusion calls it quartic although the defensible general statement is degree at most four, as the body later says. An authoritative locator is also absent, so the exact formulation cannot yet be accepted.

children.title: Angle-Difference Limit Models
children.top_down_role: Polynomial constraints representing voltage-angle differences across branches.

assumptions_latex: The endpoint voltages are nonzero and satisfy \(\operatorname{Re}(V_i\overline V_j)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounded angle difference is equivalent to two quadratic tangent inequalities together with a positive-dot-product condition.

notation.meaning: Real part of the voltage cross-product
Imaginary part of the voltage cross-product
Voltage-angle difference from i to j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tangent is monotone on the specified half-plane angle interval
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial angle-difference model restricted to the positive voltage cross-product half-plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_{ij}=e_ie_j+f_if_j\) and \(s_{ij}=f_ie_j-e_if_j\), so that \(V_i\overline V_j=c_{ij}+\mathrm{i}s_{ij}\). Under \(c_{ij}>0\), the constraint \[\underline\delta_{ij}\le\arg(V_i)-\arg(V_j)\le\overline\delta_{ij}\] is equivalent to \[s_{ij}-\tan(\underline\delta_{ij})c_{ij}\ge0,\qquad \tan(\overline\delta_{ij})c_{ij}-s_{ij}\ge0,\qquad c_{ij}>0.\] Replacing the last strict inequality by \(c_{ij}\ge\varepsilon\) for fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) yields a closed basic semialgebraic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the positive cross-product half-plane, angle-difference bounds are equivalent to two quadratic tangent inequalities and a positivity condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Angle-Difference Limit Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but equivalence depends on a precise principal-angle or modulo-2pi convention that is not stated or sourced. The model with c_{ij}>0 is not closed; only the separately proposed epsilon-strengthened variant is basic closed semialgebraic and is not exactly equivalent to positivity without an additional margin assumption.

children.title: Coupled Line-Operating Limits
children.top_down_role: Branch regimes combining flow, thermal, or angle restrictions on the same network elements.

assumptions_latex: Branch-flow, thermal, and angle-difference constraints use a common rectangular voltage vector.
Every monitored branch has fixed electrical parameters, ratings, and angle bounds satisfying the selected angle convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The simultaneous line-operating region is the intersection of the corresponding polynomial constraint sets.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: simultaneous polynomial operating limits form an intersection of basic semialgebraic branch sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint branch-flow, thermal, and angle restrictions across all monitored line ends.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each monitored directed branch \((i,j)\in\mathcal A\), define \[t_{ij}=\overline S_{ij}^{\,2}-P_{ij}^2-Q_{ij}^2,\quad a_{ij}^{-}=s_{ij}-\tan(\underline\delta_{ij})c_{ij},\quad a_{ij}^{+}=\tan(\overline\delta_{ij})c_{ij}-s_{ij}.\] The coupled line-operating region is \[\mathcal L=\left\{(e,f):t_{ij}\ge0,\ a_{ij}^{-}\ge0,\ a_{ij}^{+}\ge0,\ c_{ij}\ge\varepsilon_{ij}\ \text{for all }(i,j)\in\mathcal A\right\},\] where \(\varepsilon_{ij}>0\) enforces the chosen angle branch. Thus all line limits remain coupled through their shared bus-voltage variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The line-operating region jointly enforces flow definitions, thermal ratings, angle bounds, and angle-branch conditions using shared endpoint voltages.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Line-Operating Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is appropriate, but the plain statement says that flow definitions are jointly enforced while the displayed set only uses already-substituted flow polynomials. The epsilon angle-branch restriction also requires an explicit modeling assumption and source. No OPF citation with a specific locator is supplied.

assumptions_latex: Each generator \(i\) has active output \(P_i^g\) and a prescribed univariate polynomial cost \(c_i\).
Active generation is either explicit or represented by its rectangular-voltage injection polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The total generation cost is polynomial in the selected OPF variables.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite sums and polynomial compositions preserve polynomiality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable polynomial active-generation costs, including the standard quadratic case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For generator set \(\mathcal G\), let \[c_i(p)=\sum_{r=0}^{d_i}c_{ir}p^r\] be the prescribed cost of generator \(i\). The total objective is \[C(P^g)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal G}c_i(P_i^g).\] If active generation is eliminated through the rectangular-coordinate identity \(P_i^g=P_i^d+P_i(e,f)\), then \[C(e,f)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal G}c_i\bigl(P_i^d+P_i(e,f)\bigr)\] is again a polynomial. When \(P_i(e,f)\) is quadratic, its degree is at most \(2\max_{i\in\mathcal G}d_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing univariate polynomial generator costs gives a polynomial objective; substituting quadratic voltage-based injections preserves polynomiality and controls its degree.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Generation-Cost Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the generation-cost topic, and polynomial composition gives the stated degree upper bound. A source is required for the OPF-specific cost and elimination convention, particularly because the formulation alternates between explicit generation variables and voltage-eliminated generation.

assumptions_latex: The network graph \(G=(N,E)\) is connected and acyclic.
The AC equations and operating limits are written using bus voltages or equivalent branch-flow variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every non-root bus has a unique parent, so branch equations admit an orientation away from one root without cycle-consistency constraints.

notation.meaning: Unique parent of a non-root bus

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: connected acyclic graphs have unique simple paths and rooted parent orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural polynomial OPF regime on a connected tree network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A radial-network OPF model is an AC OPF model whose underlying undirected graph \(G=(N,E)\) is a tree. After selecting a root \(r\), each bus \(i\ne r\) has a unique parent \(\pi(i)\), and every edge can be oriented as \((\pi(i),i)\). Consequently, polynomial power-balance and branch-flow constraints can be indexed along unique root-to-bus paths, and no additional independent cycle-consistency equations are required. This structural statement does not by itself imply convexity or exactness of any relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A radial OPF network is a tree: rooting it gives every non-root bus one parent and removes independent cycle-consistency constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Radial-Network OPF Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly identifies the rooted-tree structure and appropriately avoids claiming relaxation exactness. The assertion that no additional cycle-consistency equations are required is formulation-dependent for branch-local variables and needs an authoritative radial-OPF source with an exact locator.

assumptions_latex: The network graph \(G=(N,E)\) is connected and contains at least one cycle.
The AC OPF variables include bus voltages or branch quantities intended to represent a common voltage state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent cycle relations are necessary for branch-local variables to correspond globally to bus voltage angles.

notation.meaning: Oriented voltage-angle difference on an edge

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: connected meshed graphs have nonzero cycle rank and require cycle consistency for edge phase differences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural OPF regime for connected networks with nontrivial cycle space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A meshed-network OPF model has a connected graph \(G=(N,E)\) with cycle rank \(\beta=|E|-|N|+1>0\). For branch-local phase differences to arise from bus angles, every oriented cycle \(C\) must satisfy \[\sum_{(i,j)\in C}\delta_{ij}=2\pi k_C\] for some integer \(k_C\), with signs determined by the cycle orientation. Equivalently, a voltage-product formulation must impose compatible polynomial relations around a cycle basis. Nodal power balance and individual branch limits alone do not enforce this global cycle consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A meshed OPF network has independent cycles, so branch-local phase or voltage-product variables require additional cycle-consistency relations.
knowledge_statements.title: Meshed-Network OPF Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is a reasonable role for global consistency in meshed branch-local formulations. However, the integer cycle equation depends on whether edge differences are wrapped or unwrapped, and the claimed equivalent polynomial cycle relations are not actually stated. These formulation-sensitive claims require a specific meshed-OPF source.

assumptions_latex: Every objective and constraint polynomial is expressed in a common scalar variable vector \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\).
Variable interaction is defined by simultaneous occurrence in a polynomial monomial or constraint support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting correlative sparsity graph localizes each polynomial to a clique containing its variable support.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: correlative sparsity graphs encode joint variable occurrence in polynomial optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-interaction graph induced by local OPF polynomial supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an OPF polynomial program in scalar variables \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), its correlative sparsity graph is \(G_c=(X,E_c)\), where \(X=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{r,s\}\in E_c\) whenever \(x_r\) and \(x_s\) occur together in the support of an objective term or constraint polynomial. Because bus-injection polynomials involve a bus and its neighbors while branch polynomials involve branch endpoints, network locality induces sparse supports. A chordal extension may then assign every polynomial to a maximal clique containing its variable support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlative sparsity connects variables that occur together in an OPF polynomial; network locality therefore yields small supports that can be covered by chordal cliques.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Correlative Sparsity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct content kind, but the edge rule ambiguously mixes monomial co-occurrence with whole-constraint support. Under a monomial-only rule, a polynomial's complete variable support need not form a clique, so the maximal-clique assignment does not follow as written. A specific sparse polynomial-optimization or OPF source is required to fix the intended convention.

children.title: Transmission OPF Models
children.top_down_role: Polynomial OPF model families for high-voltage transmission networks.

assumptions_latex: A balanced positive-sequence transmission network is represented by its bus-admittance matrix and rectangular bus voltages.
Loads, generator bounds, voltage bounds, and branch ratings are fixed data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transmission AC OPF is a polynomial optimization problem with quadratic balance equations and polynomial operating inequalities.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: balanced rectangular-coordinate transmission AC OPF has polynomial injections, costs, and operating limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balanced positive-sequence transmission AC OPF in rectangular voltage coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=(e,f)\) collect rectangular transmission-bus voltages, with one angle reference imposed by a linear condition such as \(f_r=0\). A polynomial transmission OPF has the form \[\min_x\ C(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad h_
u(x)=0\ \text{for all }\nu,\qquad g_\mu(x)\ge0\ \text{for all }\mu.\] Here \(h\) contains active and reactive nodal balance equations, while \(g\) contains voltage-magnitude, generation, thermal-flow, and angle-difference limits. Under the rectangular AC network model, balance equations are quadratic and the standard squared apparent-power limits are quartic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced transmission AC OPF is a polynomial program combining rectangular-voltage balance equations, generation and voltage bounds, branch limits, a reference condition, and polynomial cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Transmission OPF Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the transmission-OPF leaf, but x=(e,f) omits explicit generator variables while h is said to contain nodal balance equations. If generation is eliminated, the statement must explain which buses retain fixed-injection equalities and how generator injections become bounded polynomial expressions. Transformer, shunt, reference-angle, and branch-limit conventions also lack an authoritative locator.

children.title: Distribution OPF Models
children.top_down_role: Polynomial OPF model families for distribution networks.

knowledge_statements.title: Distribution OPF Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular-coordinate polynomial representation for a finite distribution network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(N,E)\) be a finite distribution network with complex bus voltages \(V_i=v_i^{\mathrm r}+\mathrm i v_i^{\mathrm i}\) and fixed admittance matrix \(Y\). The AC injection equations \(S_i=V_i\overline{\sum_jY_{ij}V_j}\) become quadratic equalities in the real voltage components. Generator and voltage-magnitude limits are polynomial inequalities, and each branch limit is expressible as \((P_{ij})^2+(Q_{ij})^2\leq (s_{ij}^{\max})^2\). Consequently, minimizing a polynomial generation cost subject to these relations is a polynomial optimization model; radiality is not required for this representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In rectangular voltage coordinates, distribution-network power balance is quadratic, while voltage, generator, and apparent-power limits are polynomial constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(N,E)\) and all device sets are finite.
\(Y\) and fixed loads are given constants.
Generation costs are polynomial functions of active and reactive injections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{f(x):g_k(x)\geq0,\ h_\ell(x)=0\}\) is a polynomial optimization representation of the distribution OPF.

notation.meaning: net complex-power injection at bus i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:rectangular-coordinate AC power-flow equations and standard magnitude limits are polynomial
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but no inspectable OPF-specific citation supports the distribution-network equations and limits.

children.title: Mixed-Network Interface Models
children.top_down_role: Polynomial OPF architectures coupling transmission-scale and distribution-scale subsystems.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Network Interface Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial coupling of transmission and distribution subnetworks at boundary buses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let transmission and distribution subnetworks meet at a finite interface set \(B\). For every \(b\in B\), introduce one rectangular boundary voltage \(V_b\) and interface power variables \((P_b,Q_b)\). Impose voltage consistency by identifying the terminal voltage variables, and impose opposite power conventions through \(P_b^{\mathrm T}+P_b^{\mathrm D}=0\) and \(Q_b^{\mathrm T}+Q_b^{\mathrm D}=0\). If each subnetwork has a polynomial rectangular-coordinate OPF formulation, adjoining these linear interface equations yields a single polynomial optimization model for the mixed network.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transmission and distribution polynomial OPF models combine by equating interface voltages and balancing active and reactive interface powers.
assumptions_latex: Both subnetworks use compatible voltage bases and sign conventions.
Each subnetwork model is polynomial in its local variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\mathrm T}\cap K_{\mathrm D}\cap K_B\) is a polynomial feasible set, where \(K_B\) is defined by the interface equalities.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:network decomposition uses voltage consistency and power-conservation equalities
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source supports the interface construction. A source should also clarify the relationship between the single boundary voltage and the transmission/distribution terminal variables, and define the superscripted interface powers.

children.title: Network-Regime Transfer Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits on transferring a polynomial OPF representation between network regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Regime Transfer Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for transferring a polynomial OPF template between network regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Changing a finite AC network from transmission to distribution parameters, topology, or orientation preserves the polynomial OPF class whenever admittances remain fixed and all device laws and limits are polynomial in finitely many rectangular-coordinate variables. The transfer fails as a direct polynomial model when the new regime introduces an unmodeled discrete topology decision, a nonalgebraic control law, or division by a variable that may vanish. Polynomial status can be recovered only by a valid finite lifting, including the required domain restrictions and any discrete polynomial equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A network-regime change preserves polynomial OPF exactly while all added laws admit a valid finite polynomial formulation.
assumptions_latex: The network and device index sets are finite.
Every denominator cleared during reformulation is known to be nonzero on the feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{transfer preserves polynomiality}\iff\text{all transferred constraints admit an equivalent finite polynomial formulation}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:finite polynomial equalities and inequalities define the polynomial optimization class
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary claim has no citation, and the stated equivalence requires a precise definition of polynomial representability, including projections, discrete encodings, and domain-equivalent liftings.

children.title: Multiphase OPF Extensions
children.top_down_role: Polynomial OPF formulations for networks with explicit phase representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiphase OPF Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular-coordinate polynomial OPF for explicitly represented electrical phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each bus \(i\), let \(\Phi_i\) be its available phase set and write \(V_i^\phi=v_{i\phi}^{\mathrm r}+\mathrm i v_{i\phi}^{\mathrm i}\). With fixed multiphase admittance coefficients, \(I_i^\phi=\sum_{j,\psi}Y_{i\phi,j\psi}V_j^\psi\) is linear and \(S_i^\phi=V_i^\phi\overline{I_i^\phi}\) is quadratic in rectangular components. Phasewise power balance, voltage bounds, polynomial device models, and squared current or apparent-power limits therefore define a polynomial feasible set, including networks with missing phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit phase indexing preserves polynomial OPF because multiphase currents are linear and phase powers are quadratic in rectangular voltages.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\Phi_i\) and the network index set are finite.
All included phase-device laws have polynomial formulations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\mathrm{mp}}=\{x:g_k(x)\geq0,\ h_\ell(x)=0\}\) is a finite polynomial OPF feasible set.

children.title: Unbalanced OPF Extensions
children.top_down_role: Polynomial OPF formulations accommodating asymmetric phase conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbalanced OPF Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phase-resolved polynomial OPF without balanced-voltage or balanced-load assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unbalanced OPF assigns independent rectangular voltages, injections, loads, and limits to every present bus-phase pair \((i,\phi)\), without imposing equal magnitudes or fixed \(120\)-degree separation among phases. Neutral and mutual-coupling variables may be included through a fixed linear admittance relation. Each phase equation \(S_i^\phi=V_i^\phi\overline{I_i^\phi}\) remains quadratic, and phase-specific magnitude and equipment limits remain polynomial. Thus removing the balance assumptions enlarges the variable and constraint sets but does not itself destroy polynomial representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing independent phase voltages and injections models imbalance while retaining a polynomial rectangular-coordinate OPF formulation.
assumptions_latex: The conductor admittance model is fixed and linear.
Loads and controllable devices have polynomial phase models.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\mathrm{unb}}\) is polynomial even when \(|V_i^a|,|V_i^b|,|V_i^c|\) and phase angles are unequal.

children.title: Multiphase–Imbalance Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural effects arising when explicit phase representation meets network imbalance.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiphase–Imbalance Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: How cross-phase physics couples phase imbalance in polynomial OPF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Stack the phase voltages as \(v_i=(V_i^a,V_i^b,V_i^c)\). Off-diagonal blocks of the multiphase admittance matrix make each phase current depend on voltages of other phases, so imbalance cannot generally be represented by three independent single-phase OPFs. For any fixed linear symmetrical-component transform \(T\), an imbalance bound such as \(\lvert (Tv_i)_2\rvert^2\leq\epsilon^2\lvert (Tv_i)_1\rvert^2\) is a quadratic inequality in rectangular voltage components. Hence both physical cross-phase coupling and a squared sequence-ratio limit remain polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mutual admittances couple phases, while squared symmetrical-component imbalance limits are quadratic in rectangular voltages.
assumptions_latex: All three phase coordinates used by \(T\) are defined.
\(T\) and the admittance matrix are fixed.
The imbalance limit is expressed without dividing by a possibly zero sequence magnitude.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_{\phi\psi}\neq0\) for some \(\phi\neq\psi\) couples phase equations, while \(\lvert (Tv_i)_2\rvert^2-\epsilon^2\lvert (Tv_i)_1\rvert^2\leq0\) is polynomial.

children.title: Polynomial Representation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits governing when these extensions remain within the polynomial problem class.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Representation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion for polynomial representation of multiphase and imbalance extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite multiphase or unbalanced OPF extension belongs to the polynomial optimization class when there exist finitely many auxiliary variables \(y\) such that its feasible set is the projection of \(\{(x,y):g_k(x,y)\geq0,\ h_\ell(x,y)=0\}\), with every \(g_k\) and \(h_\ell\) polynomial. Clearing a denominator is equivalent only when its nonvanishing and sign conditions are enforced. Variable-frequency trigonometric laws, transcendental device curves, or discontinuous controls lie outside this representation unless an exact finite polynomial lifting is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extension is polynomial exactly when a finite, domain-equivalent polynomial lifting exists; unsafe denominator clearing or transcendental laws cross the boundary.
assumptions_latex: The physical network has finitely many indexed components.
Projection is taken only over explicitly introduced auxiliary variables.
Reformulations preserve the original feasible domain exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,y):g_k(x,y)\geq0,\ h_\ell(x,y)=0\}\) is the required polynomial representation criterion.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:polynomial optimization permits finite polynomial liftings and projections

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Discrete OPF Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed polynomial OPF with finite-valued operational decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed-discrete polynomial OPF is an optimization problem \(\min\{f(x,z):g_k(x,z)\geq0,\ h_\ell(x,z)=0\}\), where \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) contains continuous electrical variables, \(z\) contains finitely valued decisions such as switch states, tap positions, or commitment states, and all displayed functions are polynomial. A binary decision is imposed algebraically by \(z_j(z_j-1)=0\). A finite set \(D_j=\{d_1,\ldots,d_m\}\) is imposed by \(\prod_{r=1}^m(z_j-d_r)=0\), together with any required linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-discrete OPF augments polynomial electrical constraints with finite-valued controls encoded by polynomial equations and linking constraints.
assumptions_latex: The continuous and discrete variable vectors are finite-dimensional.
Objective and linking constraints are polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(z_j\in D_j\), and polynomial constraints define a mixed-discrete polynomial optimization problem.

children.title: Security-Constrained OPF Extensions
children.top_down_role: Polynomial OPF formulations organized around contingency-indexed operating regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Security-Constrained OPF Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-contingency polynomial representation with preventive and corrective controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a finite contingency set containing the base case. A security-constrained OPF introduces a state vector \(x^c\) for every \(c\in C\), shared preventive controls \(u\), and optional corrective controls \(w^c\). It minimizes a polynomial objective subject to polynomial AC feasibility constraints \(g_k^c(x^c,u,w^c)\geq0\), \(h_\ell^c(x^c,u,w^c)=0\) in every contingency, together with polynomial nonanticipativity, reserve, and corrective-action limits. The finite intersection of these scenario feasible sets is therefore polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Security-constrained OPF replicates polynomial network constraints over finitely many contingencies and couples them through shared or bounded corrective controls.
assumptions_latex: Each contingency has fixed topology and parameters.
Preventive and corrective coupling laws are polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\mathrm{SC}}=\bigcap_{c\in C}K_c\) with shared controls is a finite polynomial feasible set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:a finite intersection of polynomial scenario models remains polynomial

children.title: Multiperiod OPF Extensions
children.top_down_role: Polynomial OPF formulations organized across linked temporal periods.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiperiod OPF Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon polynomial OPF with intertemporal device constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=\{0,\ldots,H\}\) and \(T^-=\{0,\ldots,H-1\}\), where \(H\in\mathbb N\). Introduce network states \(x_t\) and controls \(u_t\) for every \(t\in T\). Impose a polynomial AC OPF model at every \(t\in T\), and impose polynomial consecutive-period relations for every \(t\in T^-\), such as ramp limits \(-R^-\leq p_{t+1}-p_t\leq R^+\) and storage dynamics \(e_{t+1}=e_t+\eta_c p_t^c-\eta_d^{-1}p_t^d\), with fixed nonzero efficiencies. A polynomial sum of stage and terminal costs then defines a finite-dimensional polynomial optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-horizon OPF is polynomial when every period model and cost is polynomial and all polynomial intertemporal constraints are imposed only on valid consecutive-period pairs.
assumptions_latex: Efficiencies and time-step parameters are fixed constants, with \(\eta_d\neq0\).
All period and intertemporal device models are polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{\sum_{t\in T}f_t(x_t,u_t)+f_H^{\mathrm{term}}(x_H):\text{period constraints for }t\in T,\ \text{coupling constraints for }t\in T^-\}\) is a polynomial optimization problem when all displayed functions and constraints are polynomial.

knowledge_statements.title: Contingency–Time Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling structure of finite-contingency, finite-horizon polynomial OPF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Index post-contingency states by \((c,t)\in C\times T\). Preventive decisions made before contingency revelation must satisfy nonanticipativity equalities, while corrective decisions may depend on \(c\) only after its revelation time. For each contingency, intertemporal equations link \(x_{c,t+1}\) to \((x_{c,t},u_{c,t})\); security limits apply at every indexed state. If the scenario-time models, nonanticipativity equations, and dynamics are polynomial, their joint feasible set is polynomial, although it generally does not decompose independently by contingency or time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonanticipativity couples contingencies, dynamics couple times, and their finite polynomial combination remains polynomial but generally nonseparable.
assumptions_latex: The contingency revelation convention is fixed.
All state transitions and cross-index constraints are polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=\bigcap_{(c,t)\in C\times T}K_{c,t}\cap K_{\mathrm{NA}}\cap K_{\mathrm{dyn}}\) is polynomial and generally nonseparable.

children.title: Joint Extension Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits governing polynomial representation under combined contingency-indexed temporal structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Extension Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial boundary for jointly security-constrained and multiperiod OPF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A joint contingency-time OPF has a finite-dimensional polynomial formulation when its indexed local models and all dynamics, recourse restrictions, and nonanticipativity rules admit an exact formulation using finitely many variables and polynomial equalities and inequalities. Finite sets \(C\) and \(T\), together with polynomial local and coupling laws, are sufficient for this property. An infinite or continuously parameterized uncertainty set requires an additional exact finite reduction before it yields such a formulation. Transcendental dynamics, discontinuous policies, and variable-denominator relations also require an exact finite polynomial lifting with all necessary domain conditions. Finite-valued controls yield a mixed-discrete polynomial model rather than a purely continuous polynomial model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint contingency-time extensions are finite polynomial models when the complete exact formulation has finitely many variables and polynomial local and coupling constraints; finite indexing is sufficient, while infinite indexing requires an exact finite reduction.
assumptions_latex: The intended model is exact rather than a sampled approximation.
Every reformulation preserves the original feasible domain.
Every discrete domain included in the formulation is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) and \(T\) finite with polynomial local and coupling laws implies a finite polynomial formulation; an infinite index family has this property only if an exact finite polynomial reduction is available.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:finite polynomial systems remain polynomial under finite conjunction and lifting
